title: Analysis of conflicts of interest among authors and researchers of European clinical guidelines in cardiovascular medicine
authors: Hinton J, Reeves T, Shah BN
population: Committee authors of five European Society of Cardiology guidelines (valvular heart disease, atrial fibrillation, pericardial diseases, heart failure and myocardial revascularisation) and the funding of studies cited in their drug-related recommendations
funder: not stated: the full text on PubMed Central carries no funding or competing-interest statement.
result: Of 603 recommendations, 271 (45%) concerned pharmaceutical agents, 72 of 169 in the heart failure guideline. In every guideline except pericardial diseases, at least 80% of committee authors had a relevant financial conflict of interest, most often a direct personal payment (68 to 82%). Industry support of cited studies ranged from 5% to 65% across guidelines, and when a cited study was industry-funded its authors were conflicted with the sponsor in 55 to 90% of cases. The authors propose that guideline writers be free of such conflicts.
